How the rows decide where to run:

Bit for bit:
- WAV reader against wavio.read_wav, at 8 kHz: every sample's bits, NaN payloads included for one channel. Checked on about 100 corner files, 3000 fuzzed files and 800 well-formed random-byte files. In the fuzz, 501 files read OK and the rest were refused under every exception class. 147 of the 800 well-formed files raised numpy RuntimeWarnings, and 653 were multichannel.
- Exception class and text exactly, and the warning list (category and text, in order) exactly.
- When resampled (16000, 11025 Hz, a later fmt chunk at 16 kHz): within 1e-12 of the scale, as the author's bar. Measured worst 0 in the corner set.
- _owned: same booleans and same errors, including Python's unpacking messages and laziness.
- Typed scenarios: unchanged bars, and now proven typed (0 calls reach the per-pass bindings through Python).

Not compared:
- The NaN payload of a multichannel mean where one frame holds several NaNs. Which payload survives depends on the compiler's operand order (found by the fuzz; see deviations).
- Exotic huge sizes where numpy runs out of memory.
deviations: When one frame holds several NaNs, the channel mean can carry a different NaN payload. Position, sign of non-NaN values and every other bit agree. x86 addsd passes on the first operand's payload, and GCC commutes `+` freely in numpy's build and in ours, so numpy's choice is a property of its build. Measured: row 10 of fuzz case 121 (float16, 17 channels, two sNaNs) gave numpy 0xfffe340000000000 and C++ 0xfffa280000000000.

np.fromfile allocates the declared element count before reading. For a data size numpy cannot allocate, the reference raises MemoryError (seen for an RF64 data size of 2**40 with 3-byte samples: _ArrayMemoryError, 1 TiB). The C++ reads what is in the file. The fuzz keeps RF64 sizes allocatable.

If the resampling factor rate/gcd(8000, rate) exceeds (INT_MAX-1)/20, the C++ throws std::bad_alloc (MemoryError) before resample_poly's int tap count would overflow. scipy would try to design a filter of billions of taps.

A 64-bit float in a 16-byte container is read as numpy's long double, which is platform-defined. Where long double is 16 bytes (x86-64 Linux/macOS: x87 extended; aarch64 Linux: quad), the C++ uses the platform's own long double cast and fenv flags, so values and warnings match numpy there. On Windows and macOS arm64 it is TypeError "data type '<f16' not understood", as numpy refuses it there. A MinGW build is forced to the Windows behaviour.

_owned's binding converts each a3 entry's three items with float() when it unpacks the entry. The reference subtracts lazily: it touches cc only if the line test fails, and zz only if the entry is kept. A non-numeric entry can therefore raise in C++ where Python short-circuits, or raise ValueError where Python raises TypeError (e.g. 'abc'). a3 always comes from _a3_lines (floats).
WavFileWarning and RuntimeWarning are emitted at stacklevel 1 from the binding's caller, not scipy's stacklevel 2 (cosmetic).
shared_changes_needed: Paths are narrow std::string handed to fopen across the QRSS core (wavread.cpp, wav.cpp, api.cpp, npz.cpp, beaconfile.cpp). On Windows/MSVC a non-ASCII path (e.g. C:\Users\Jose-with-accent\...) is read through the ANSI code page and will not open. Separately, the bindings encode a str path with surrogatepass where Python's open() uses os.fsencode (surrogateescape), so a Linux filename that is not UTF-8 is not found from Python. Both need a project-wide path convention (UTF-8 to _wfopen / std::filesystem::path, and PyUnicode_EncodeFSDefault in the bindings); not changed here.

receiver_slot_review.notes: Review of f6a9124. The main problem was the WAV reader, which differed from scipy.io.wavfile.read in many ways. It is rewritten as a faithful model of scipy's walk: a position-modelled fid, struct.unpack-sized reads, numpy dtype choice by container, fromfile consumption, and refusals and warnings mapped to the reference's Python classes. The orchestration itself (flow template, Typed/Py policies, budget, merges, rules) re-read clean: no operation-order, tie or seam differences found beyond _owned's eagerness. Probes added: WAV corners, fuzz and value fuzz; refusals through capture_from_wav and receive_wav; _owned laziness; a typed-really-typed spy in _run; C++ reader checks in the ctest. The slow tier was not re-run; none of the slow scenarios read WAVs, and the binding changes outside the reader are _owned and receive_wav's argument order. No push.

findings.what: wav::read_wav ignored the RIFF size field and stopped at the first data chunk, where scipy reads chunks only while tell() < RIFF size + 8, reads every chunk after data, returns the LAST data chunk and the LAST fmt chunk's rate. So a header with size 0 or too small (streaming writers) was read by C++ but refused by the reference (UnboundLocalError). With two data chunks, C++ returned the first.
There was no PCM nAvgBytesPerSec == nSamplesPerSec * nBlockAlign check. scipy refuses such headers with a ValueError; the C++ read them.

PCM containers scipy reads were refused: 5-7 bytes (left-justified int64, / 2**63-1), 8 bytes (int64), a 1-byte container of more than 8 bits or 0 bits (int8 / 127), 8-bit samples in a wider container (scipy's contiguous-bytes quirk), and bps 3 with bits over 64. Float sample types were chosen by bit depth rather than container, so float16 (2-byte), float64 in a '32-bit' chunk, float32 in a '64-bit' chunk and 16-byte long double were refused or misread.

WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE took the subformat as a u16 at the GUID with no check of the GUID's standard tail. scipy requires the tail (else 'Unknown wave file format: EXTENSIBLE'), reads the subformat as uint32 (a 0x10001 subformat is refused, not PCM), and requires cbSize >= 22 when the fmt chunk is at least 18 bytes. A non-standard GUID was decoded as PCM by C++.
RIFX (big-endian) and RF64 files were refused although scipy reads both.

Refusals were std::invalid_argument('unsupported WAV: ...'), which became ValueError with the C++'s own text. The reference raises struct.error, ZeroDivisionError, TypeError (numpy dtype), UnboundLocalError and ValueError with scipy's texts and format names. Now wav::FormatError carries the class, and the binding raises the reference's class and text.

scipy's WavFileWarnings and numpy's RuntimeWarnings were never emitted. These cover unknown chunks, premature EOF, incomplete chunk IDs, float32 sNaN casts, the long-double cast, and the channel mean's overflow and invalid flags. They are now collected in order and warned by the binding.
A path containing a NUL byte was truncated by fopen, which opened the prefix file. Python's open() raises ValueError('embedded null byte').

The receive_wav binding converted q, start_unix, spec and estimator before reading the file. The reference reads the file first, so a missing file plus a bad q raised TypeError/ValueError instead of FileNotFoundError.

The _owned binding unpacked and converted every a3 entry eagerly. The reference unpacks a3 only when a preamble-found signal owns the band, once per owner, so a generator a3 is spent by the first owner. A malformed entry raised in C++ where the reference returns False. Non-iterable entries raised the wrong text ('object is not iterable' vs 'cannot unpack non-iterable object object'), and an infinite iterator entry would hang. Python 3.13's unpack messages are now reproduced.

Tests: the typed scenarios asserted only the `typed` flag handed to the binding, so a silent fallback (Untyped) to the Python objects would have passed unnoticed. A spy on the per-pass bindings now proves typed runs never reach Python stages.
The ctest Stub aggregate initialisations produced about 30 -Wmissing-field-initializers warnings (log, passes, detected had no default member initialisers).

The NaN payload of a multichannel mean over several NaNs is not reproduced. It is decided by compiler operand order in numpy's build and in ours, so it cannot be matched reliably. Documented and excluded from the bit-for-bit comparison.

review.notes: Review of the sstvae-qrss receive port (qrss_receive.py --no-store vs sstvae-qrss receive). I worked in the existing worktree and reused native/build-qrss and native/build-qrss-codec; nothing was pushed. The commit adds only the six files listed, with the required trailers. sstvae/ and the other shared files are untouched: a temporary CMake hook used to exercise --image was reverted, and the codec tree was rebuilt without it. Two real bugs were fixed: q < 0 now gives the reference's ValueError, and the simfile str width is read without overflow. The negative-q fix is mutation-checked, and two refusal cases pin it. The remaining items are shared edits I was not allowed to make, listed in shared_changes_needed. The most important is the receiver.cpp q < 0 throw, because api::receive_slot (and therefore listen) still wraps q; only the CLI is guarded today. The other two that matter are the --image CMake line and the stale test_dispatch pin. Minor, not fixed: receive.cpp carries its own copy of pathlib_str, a duplicate of qc::pathlib_str, which is unavoidable without linking the codec library. A --start past year 2255 double-rounds its seconds. Scratch probes are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-sstvae/92006b74-04c2-5210-829f-64b8a831fdbf/scratchpad/rv/.

findings.what: A slot before 1970 (q < 0, from --slot or the .npz) made the C++ print a pass while qrss_receive.py exits 1 with 'ValueError: q must fit in uint64, not -N'. The native demodulators cast q to uint64 and wrap it. receive.cpp now returns the reference's error whenever a pass is found, and refusal cases slot-before-1970 and npz-q-negative pin it (mutation-checked). The in-process API still wraps q; the core fix in receiver.cpp is listed as a shared change.

simfile str_member read the '<U<n>' width with std::stoul (32-bit on MSVC, throws out_of_range) and formed 4 * width unchecked: at >= 2^62 it wraps, skips the short-member check, and allocates. A short member's text also differed from numpy's ('npy: EOF reading ...' vs 'EOF: reading array data, ...'). Now an overflow-safe digit loop with numpy's text; pins frame_wide, frame_one_over and frame_huge were added from Python, and the last is a recorded deviation for its message text.
The new simfile pin generator cases used zipfile.writestr, which stamps the clock time, so regenerating simfile_pins.hpp was nondeterministic. They now write members as np.savez does.

--image is never compiled into sstvae-qrss: receive_image.cpp needs a target_sources line in native/CMakeLists.txt (a shared file). Without it the codec build refuses --image and the image parity tests skip.
tests/test_qrss_native_cli.py:335-336 test_dispatch still pins 'receive: not in this build yet' and fails now that receive is built (shared test); main.cpp's NOT_BUILT receive entry is dead.

After merging d9f3350 (wav::FormatError), receive.cpp's catch of std::invalid_argument maps every WAV format error to ValueError. It needs a FormatError catch first, mapping kind to struct.error, ZeroDivisionError, TypeError or UnboundLocalError.

The decimal-comma locale test cannot fail from either protective layer alone. In a build without the fetcher it holds by construction; in the fetch build, removing main's LC_NUMERIC reset still passes because py_format maps the point itself (measured). The docstring now says so; a py_format locale ctest is suggested.

Minor: fs=0 gives ValueError (simfile) where Python gives ZeroDivisionError; a 2-D fe gives a clearer ValueError than numpy's; Python's numpy and WAV warnings on stderr are not reproduced; a --start past year 2255 double-rounds; receive.cpp duplicates qc::pathlib_str. All are accepted deviations or cosmetic.
